title: "Shall I Show You…": The One Sentence the Deceiver and the Guide Both Use
excerpt: The offer of guidance — hal adulluka/kum ʿalā, 'shall I show you the way to…' (root d-l-l) — is spoken in the Quran by Shaytan luring Adam (20:120), by Musa's sister inside Pharaoh's palace (28:12), and by God calling the believers (61:10). One identical sentence, three fingers pointing. The counterfeit of guidance uses guidance's own opening line — and the only tell is the direction the finger points.
seo_title: Shall I Show You: When the Deceiver Borrows Guidance's Own Words (20:120, 28:12, 61:10)
seo_description: The phrase 'shall I show you the way to…' (hal adulluka, root d-l-l) is used by Shaytan (20:120), Musa's sister (28:12), and God (61:10). A corpus-verified reading of how the counterfeit of guidance copies its grammar exactly — and how to tell them apart.
